description: Structure and function of the human body systems and organs

body_overview.cells: ~37 trillion; basic structural and functional units
body_overview.bones: 206 in adult; 270–300 in newborns (fuse over time)
body_overview.height_weight: Average adult 170 cm, 70 kg; varies widely by sex and population

divisions.axial: 80 bones; skull, vertebral column, rib cage
divisions.appendicular: 126 bones; limbs, shoulder and hip girdles

major_bones.vertebrae: 33 total; 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral (fused), 4 coccygeal (fused)

major_muscles.quadriceps: 4 muscles on front of thigh; extend knee

heart.rate: 60–100 BPM normal; cardiac output ~5 L/min at rest
heart.electrical: SA node (pacemaker) → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibers

blood_vessels.arteries: Carry blood away from heart; thick walls
blood_vessels.veins: Carry blood to heart; valves prevent backflow
blood_vessels.capillaries: Exchange of gases, nutrients, waste at tissue level

blood.rh_factor: Positive or negative; important for pregnancy and transfusions

nervous_system.cns: Central Nervous System; brain and spinal cord
nervous_system.pns: Peripheral Nervous System; all other nerves

brain_regions.cerebrum: Largest part; conscious thought, movement, sensation, memory
brain_regions.brainstem: Controls automatic functions (breathing, heart rate, blood pressure)

neurons.structure: Cell body, dendrites (receive signals), axon (send signals)

digestive_system.path: Mouth → Esophagus → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine → Rectum → Anus
digestive_system.stomach: Acid pH 1.5–3.5; churns food; pepsin breaks proteins
digestive_system.small_intestine: ~6 m; absorption of nutrients; duodenum, jejunum, ileum
digestive_system.large_intestine: ~1.5 m; water absorption; bacteria ferment remaining material
digestive_system.liver: Largest internal organ; metabolizes drugs and toxins; produces bile

key_glands.pituitary: Master gland; controls other glands; growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH
key_glands.pancreas: Insulin (lowers blood sugar), glucagon (raises blood sugar)
